searchHelp.title: How to search
searchHelp.subtitle: Search by title, author, translator, publisher or year. Adding words narrows the results.
searchHelp.accents: Accents may be omitted or included; this returns Angústia.
searchHelp.misspelling: Minor misspellings are tolerated when no exact match is found, here and within an operator alike.
searchHelp.prefix: An incomplete word matches any word beginning with it, such as Machado.
searchHelp.titleField: Restricts the search to the title, excluding matches elsewhere in the record.
searchHelp.authorField: The author of the original work.
searchHelp.publisherField: Also country:, original: for the original title, and source: for the sources a record cites.
searchHelp.rangeField: A range. year:2000- runs from that year onwards, and year:-1900 up to it.
searchHelp.phrase: Quotation marks match the words in the order given.
searchHelp.allWords: Parentheses match all the words, in any order, and like any other word allowing for a misspelling.
searchHelp.exclude: A leading minus sign excludes matching records.
searchHelp.repeat: Repeating an operator requires both conditions to hold.
searchHelp.either: Returns records matching either side, rather than both.

about.label: About the platform
about.heading: About the <break></break><name>Richard & Isabel Burton Platform</name>
about.burtons: The platform is named after the first known translators of a book of Brazilian literature into English. Sir Richard Francis Burton (1821-1890), and his wife Isabel Burton (1831-1896) are considered the pioneers in translating Brazilian literature into English. They had contact with author José de Alencar and his literary works while Sir Burton served as British consul in Santos, Brazil (1865-1868). The English translation for <iracema>Iracema, The Honey-lips: A legend of Brazil</iracema> (1886), by José de Alencar, was first published by Bickers and Son publishing house, in London. After this first step, hundreds of books of literature have been translated into English with the efforts of independent translators, literary agents, publishing houses, and universities, making Brazilian literature available to the Anglophone readership.
about.readMore: Read more about Richard & Isabel Burton at <burtoniana>burtoniana.org</burtoniana> and <museum>sir richard burton museum.co.uk</museum>.
about.browse: Browse books translated by Richard & Isabel Burton <here>here</here>
about.platform: The <name>Richard & Isabel Burton Platform</name> is an open access online repository with reliable data about Brazilian literature in translation to English, stemmed from the need to preserve the Brazilian cultural and historical heritage as well as its international dissemination. The platform intends to contribute to translation flows worldwide, facilitating the access of Brazilian literature to Anglophone readers and researchers.
about.registered: The first version of the platform was registered by the <ifrs>Federal Institute of Education, Science and Technology of Rio Grande do Sul (IFRS)</ifrs> in 2016, linked to the project <project>“Brazilian Literature and Transnationalities: Displacements, Identities and Technological Experiments”</project>, with the goal of serving as a tool for readers, researchers, academic and governmental institutions interested in accessing data on works of Brazilian literature translated into English. Furthermore, the platform intends to contribute to translation flows worldwide, and the promotion of Brazilian cultural heritage in Brazil and abroad, facilitating its access to Anglophone readers and researchers.
about.current: The current version has been developed since 2022, through the research project <project>“Brazilian Literature in Translation: Solutions in Science and Technology”</project>, with support of the <fapergs>Foundation of Research Support of the Rio Grande do Sul State (Fapergs)</fapergs> and <wyeworks>WyeWorks</wyeworks>’s collaboration.
about.scope: The <name>R&I</name> platform’s data collection includes titles of books from Brazilian literature translated into English. It doesn’t include titles of anthologies, collections or works published in magazines, newspapers and/or electronic media.
